valid_fixes: Change AnalyticsFunction.Environment.Variables.BUCKET_NAME from !Ref InventoryTable to !Ref AnalyticsBucket so the env var resolves to the S3 bucket name instead of the DynamoDB table name
invalid_patches: Grant s3:PutObject on '*' to AnalyticsRole — this does not fix the NoSuchBucket error caused by the wrong bucket name
Create an S3 bucket named after the stack's inventory table to match the wrong env var — adds a spurious bucket instead of correcting the reference
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_check_queue_depth(queue=AnalyticsJobEventsQueue) → messages draining, function is being invoked
ace_get_environment_variables(function=AnalyticsFunction) → BUCKET_NAME resolves to ace-bench-stack-inventory, not ace-bench-stack-analytics
ace_get_stack_outputs() → AnalyticsBucketName=ace-bench-stack-analytics, InventoryTableName=ace-bench-stack-inventory — confirms BUCKET_NAME points to DynamoDB table name not S3 bucket
observable_symptom: The analytics function is invoked and the analytics queue drains, but no objects appear in object storage. Function logs show NoSuchBucket errors on every invocation. The BUCKET_NAME environment variable resolves to the inventory database's physical name rather than the analytics storage location name.
root_cause: AnalyticsFunction.Environment.Variables.BUCKET_NAME is set to !Ref InventoryTable instead of !Ref AnalyticsBucket. CloudFormation resolves !Ref InventoryTable to the DynamoDB table physical name (e.g., ace-bench-stack-inventory), not the S3 bucket name (ace-bench-stack-analytics). The handler calls s3.put_object with this wrong name, raising NoSuchBucket. The AnalyticsRole policy correctly grants s3:PutObject on the real analytics bucket ARN, so IAM inspection appears normal and masks the env var misconfiguration.
